title: Introduction to Kotlin Collections
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of introduction to kotlin collections using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates introduction to kotlin collections.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Introduction to Kotlin Collections** as part of **Strings, Arrays, and Collections**. Select a collection by the invariants you need—ordering, uniqueness, key lookup, or indexed access—and check the cost of transformations. Use the subtopics—Collection Interfaces, Read-Only and Mutable Collections, Choosing a Collection Type—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

items.title: Collection Interfaces
items.text: Collection Interfaces is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A read-only collection reference proves that no code can mutate the underlying data.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
